what_happened: The person running Athena wrote a request to fix verifier evidence. They scoped it to "planned demonstrations". The demo runner it produced reads its demonstrations from the plan. Easy jobs skip planning and have no plan, so they have no demonstrations. The job-slot fix was an easy job. It was rejected a third time for the same missing proof. This is an intervention note, not a failed job record.
cause: Athena does not check a request that changes how the verifier gets its evidence against the rules that judge the verifier's output, or against every path a job can take. The writer is not shown which job shapes exist: planned, or easy with no plan. Nothing compares the request's scope with those shapes before it is queued. So a fix built for one path is accepted as complete. The gap shows only when a job on the uncovered path is rejected again. This is the same missing cross-check as the earlier verifier-evidence cases. Each fix was written from memory of one path.
prevention: Add a check before dispatch for any request or reading that changes verifier evidence rules or the demo runner. It lists every job path (planned and unplanned) and every criterion kind that reaches the verifier. It requires the request to name how evidence is produced on each path, or to say explicitly that a path is out of scope. A replay should also run the evidence rule on one recent job from each path. In particular, a job with no plan must still get demonstrations or an accepted equivalent. The fix itself must give no-plan jobs a source of demonstrations, for example from the reading's criteria.
proposed_request:
Make the verifier's behavior-criterion evidence work for every job, including easy jobs that skip planning and have no plan.

Outcome: a job whose criteria need run-time proof gets that proof whether or not it was planned. Today the demo runner reads demonstrations only from the plan, so unplanned jobs have none and are rejected for missing evidence. The job-slot fix was rejected three times for this reason.

Acceptance:
- For a job with no plan, the demo runner derives demonstrations from the accepted reading's criteria, or the verifier is allowed to run the checks itself. Either way, each behavior criterion has a command the verifier saw running and lists in its structured commands field.
- A test runs the evidence rule on an unplanned job with a behavior criterion. It passes with the new path and fails without it.
- A test runs the same rule on a planned job and shows it behaves as before.
- Before the change is accepted, the evidence rule is replayed on one recent planned job and one recent unplanned job. The result is shown in the job report.
- The re-queued job-slot fix is run afterwards as a check, with no change to its request.
